analysis: What changed vs the 4 AM brief: the giveback widened steadily through the morning — S&P futures went from -0.46% at 5:26 AM ET to about -1.0% by the latest prints, Nasdaq-100 from -1.11% to about -1.9% — so this is not a one-off open dip but a morning-long fade, still concentrated in Monday's winners. Nvidia is the axis: -5.2% premarket to ~$156.40, with UBS holding a Buy and $220 target, while Trump publicly praised Blackwell as 'impossible to pirate' — political cover and analyst support are not stopping the re-pricing of the governance overhang. The split in earnings reactions is the day's real tell: Best Buy (+7% premarket) and Agilent (+6.8%) beat and raised and were rewarded, while HPE (-10.9%) and Semtech (-8.4%) beat and fell — the market is sorting on guide quality and demand durability, not on beats alone. A new geopolitical layer landed overnight: Bessent's Operation Economic Outcast sanctions on Iran's shadow banking ($14.7B flagged) plus the Hormuz mine reports, yet crude is still down (-0.35% WTI) — the market keeps pricing surplus over shipping risk. The macro backdrop also hardened: FedWatch now prices a 100% likelihood of a hike after the December meeting, up from ~96-99% in prior briefs. Signal vs noise: the widening futures fade, the beat-vs-guide split, and the 100% hike pricing are signal; the exact premarket percentages in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape are noise. The next real tests are today's data (consumer confidence, FOMC minutes) and Dell/HP after the close.

headlines.headline: Futures losses widened through the morning: S&P 500 futures about -1.0%, Nasdaq-100 futures about -1.9%, Dow futures about -0.5% in the latest prints (Investopedia), versus -0.46%, -1.11% and -0.14% at 5:26 AM ET (Reuters). SPY -0.35% at $719.78, QQQ -0.97% at $644.69 premarket (Benzinga).
headlines.why_it_matters: The fade is widening rather than stabilizing — sellers are active all morning, not just taking profits at the open, and the pain is concentrated in tech.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -5.2% premarket to ~$156.40 (Reuters), giving back part of Monday's 31.5% surge. UBS maintained a Buy rating and $220 target on Tuesday. President Trump said Nvidia maintains a technological advantage because Huang understands how to build advanced processors, calling Blackwell 'impossible to pirate' for China.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a presidential endorsement and a Buy rating with a $220 target are not stopping the re-pricing — the market is weighing the unresolved investigations (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony) more than the leadership return.

headlines.headline: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled a new round of Iran sanctions under Operation Economic Outcast, targeting over two dozen exchange houses, front companies and individuals; OFAC added 22 entities and 8 people. FinCEN flagged ~$14.7B in transactions (Jan 2025–Aug 2026) potentially linked to Iran's shadow banking. Iran's Fars agency said two oil tankers exploded after hitting sea mines east of the Strait of Hormuz — not independently confirmed.
headlines.why_it_matters: A fresh escalation in the Gulf pressure campaign, but crude is still lower — the market keeps pricing oil surplus over shipping risk. The mine reports are single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Best Buy Q3 FY27: revenue $10.24B (+5.8% y/y) vs ~$9.9B expected, adjusted EPS $1.62 vs $1.49 expected; comparable sales +6.1%, best in five years. Raised FY27 guidance: revenue $43.0-43.3B, adjusted EPS $6.90-7.05, comps +3.4-4.0%. Shares +7.05% premarket to $103.84 (Finnhub premarket quote).
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean beat-and-raise rewarded on a down tape — the AI gadget upgrade cycle is showing up in retail comps, and it is the morning's clearest counterweight to the chip selloff.

headlines.headline: Agilent Q4 2026: EPS $1.86 on revenue $2.04B, beating estimates, and issued FY27 and Q1 adjusted EPS and sales guidance above estimates. Shares +6.77% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat-and-raise being bought — the market is rewarding guide quality this morning, which sharpens the contrast with HPE and Semtech.

headlines.headline: Semtech Q3 FY27: EPS $1.17 on revenue $423M, beating estimates — shares still -8.43% premarket. HPE also still falling, -10.87% premarket after its beat-and-raise Monday evening.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two beats selling off in one morning confirms the bar is the guide, not the quarter — a beat alone is no longer enough in AI-adjacent hardware.

headlines.headline: Chips and memory broadly lower premarket: iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) down more than 4%, Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) down ~5%; Micron about -6%, Intel about -5.8%, AMD and Marvell down 3.3-4.3%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is sector-wide across semis and memory, not just Nvidia — Monday's rally is being unwound across the whole AI hardware complex.

headlines.headline: Dell -5.39% premarket ahead of Q3 FY27 results after the close; analysts expect EPS of $6.61 on revenue of $49.24B. HP and Workday also report after the close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dell is the next check on AI server demand and pricing after HPE's guide-driven selloff — and it is already being marked down before the print.
